title: NUPL says 7 minors from ASEAN protest still in custody; LGU says discharge process ongoing
summary: Seven minors apprehended in connection with a protest action during the November 15 opening of the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit remain in custody as of Thursday morning,…

blocks.text: Seven minors apprehended in connection with a protest action during the November 15 opening of the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit remain in custody as of Thursday morning, the National Union of Peoples' Lawyers (NUPL) said.

The NUPL disputed the Department of Justice's (DOJ) November 18 announcement that all 20 minors arrested in connection with the Lakbayan ng Timog Katagalugan protest caravan had already been released.
"As of this writing, seven (7) minors remain in custody and are still undergoing discharge conferences. None of these seven (7) minors has been released," the NUPL said in a statement.
The lawyers' group called on the DOJ to immediately correct its statement and accurately disclose the continuing detention of the minors.
Muntinlupa City Prosecutor's Office ordered the release of the anti-Trump and anti-Pax Silica protesters from detention and custody on Wednesday.

While NUPL welcomed the release of 216 protesters and journalists from Camp Bagong Diwa, along with five other minors from Bahay Pag-asa child care institution, the group called out the alleged delay in the release of seven more minors from Bahay Pag-asa.

Muntinlupa Mayor Ruffy Biazon, meanwhile, said Bahay Pag-asa had started the discharge procedures for the minors following the City Prosecutor's resolution ordering their release for further investigation.

He said the minors would be released immediately after completing the procedures, which include exit interviews, inventory of personal belongings, preparation of discharge documents, and conferences with their parents or guardians.

"Bagaman natanggap ng Bahay Pagasa ang resolusyon kahapon ng alas-singko ng hapon, matapos ang konsultasyon sa mga magulang, nagdesisyon ang BP na papahingahin muna ang mga bata at isagawa ng discharge procedure agaran ngayong umaga," he said.

(Although Bahay Pagasa received the resolution yesterday at 5 p.m., after consultation with the parents, BP decided to let the children rest first and conduct the discharge procedure immediately this morning.)
After consulting with the parents, however, the mayor said Bahay Pag-asa decided to let the minors rest before proceeding with their discharge on Thursday.

Biazon explained that Bahay Pag-asa, a facility for children in conflict with the law, follows specific procedures to ensure the minors' well-being, particularly those who may have experienced psychological stress or trauma. — VDV, GMA News
